california.name: California

rate.note: 2025 schedules: 1% to 12.3% (single: 12.3% over $742,953; MFJ over $1,485,906), plus 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1,000,000 = 13.3% combined top marginal rate. 2026 schedules not yet published on ftb.ca.gov (NON VÉRIFIÉ pour 2026).

rules: Early distributions (before age 59½) from qualified plans and IRAs are included in California income and subject to an additional 2.5% tax, figured on form FTB 3805P.
The 2.5% California tax is in addition to the federal 10% additional tax.
California generally follows federal exceptions to the early-distribution tax, but does not conform to all of them.
SIMPLE IRA distributions within the first two years of participation: 6% additional California tax.
No age-based state exclusion for retirement distributions.
quotes: The portion of the early distribution that is included in income is subject to an additional 2½% tax.

California and federal laws are generally the same for the tax on early distributions except for the rate of tax assessed. California does not conform to all of the federal exceptions to the additional tax on early distributions.
Line 4 – Multiply line 3 by 2½% (.025).
If your taxable income is more than $1,000,000, compute the Behavioral Health Services Tax
Tax rate – 1%: .01

pennsylvania.name: Pennsylvania

exclusions.covers: Distributions from an eligible Pennsylvania retirement plan (401(a) plans, IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEPs, Keogh) received after retirement once the plan's age or years-of-service conditions are met; for IRAs, when no federal early-withdrawal penalty applies (e.g. age 59½).
exclusions.note: No dollar cap. Not an age-based exclusion: it depends on the plan's retirement conditions. 403(b)/457(b) not named explicitly on the page read (NON VÉRIFIÉ).

rules: Retirement benefits from an eligible Pennsylvania retirement plan paid after retirement, once the plan's age or service conditions are met, are not taxable.
Distributions before the plan's retirement age or years of service are taxable to the extent they exceed previously taxed contributions.
Employee contributions to retirement plans are taxed as compensation when made, so early distributions are taxed only above that basis (cost recovery method: basis comes out first).
IRA distributions are exempt when no federal early-withdrawal penalty is owed; otherwise taxable above previously taxed contributions.
quotes: Distributions from an eligible Pennsylvania retirement plan before retirement age or years of service are taxable in the year received to the extent that the distributions exceed previously taxed contributions.
Early distributions are deemed to come from previously taxed contributions first (cost recovery method).
Employee contributions to any retirement plan are always taxable as compensation.
the department will consider the distributions exempt retirement income so long as the taxpayer is not required to pay a penalty for early withdrawal.
Tax Year Rate 2004 – Present 3.07%

illinois.name: Illinois

rate.note: tax.illinois.gov: 'Effective July 1, 2017: 4.95 percent of net income' (current rates page).

exclusions.covers: Federally taxed distributions from qualified employee benefit plans (IRC 402-408, incl. 401(k)), IRAs, SEP, state/local governmental 457 plans, government retirement; subtracted on IL-1040 line 5.
exclusions.note: Any age, no cap; early distributions included. Not covered: non-government deferred compensation plans (e.g. a private 457(b)) per Pub. 120.

rules: Illinois lets residents subtract the federally taxed portion of distributions from qualified plans (including 401(k)) and IRAs, at any age.
Early distributions from qualified plans and IRAs can be subtracted too.
Only state or local governmental 457 plans qualify; deferred compensation plans that are not government plans do not.
quotes: You may include early distributions from qualified plans and IRAs.
a qualified employee benefit plan including 401(k) plans
A qualified employee benefit plan is defined in Internal Revenue Code (IRC) Sections 402 through 408.
The Illinois income tax rate is 4.95 percent (.0495).

mississippi.name: Mississippi

rate.note: First $10,000 of taxable income at 0%; excess taxed at 4% in 2026 (4.4% in 2025, 3.75% in 2027).

exclusions.covers: Retirement income from federal, state and private retirement systems, when the recipient has met the plan's retirement requirements.
exclusions.note: No age floor and no cap stated; distributions taxable as early distributions under the IRC (Form 5329) do not qualify.

rules: Retirement income is generally exempt in Mississippi once the recipient meets the retirement plan requirements.
Early distributions are not retirement income for Mississippi and are taxable.
Pensions and annuities taxable as early or excess distributions under the Internal Revenue Code (Form 5329) do not qualify for the exemption.
Deferred compensation distributions received before the plan's retirement age and/or service requirements are taxable.
quotes: Generally, retirement income, pensions and annuities are not subject to Mississippi Income tax if the recipient has met the retirement plan requirements. Early distributions are not considered retirement income and may be subject to tax.
Pensions and annuities that are taxable as early or excess distributions under the Federal Internal Revenue Code (see Federal Form 5329) do not qualify for exemption from Mississippi income tax.
Tax Year 2026 Excess of $10,000 of Taxable Income is taxed @ 4%

iowa.name: Iowa

exclusions.covers: Pensions, annuities, traditional and Roth IRAs, SEP, SIMPLE IRA, 401(k), 403(b), 457(b), defined benefit plans, Keogh, ESOP; not nonqualified deferred compensation (409A) or nonqualified annuities.
exclusions.note: Full exclusion (no cap stated) for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2023, if age 55+ on Dec 31 of the tax year, disabled, or a qualifying survivor.

rules: Since tax year 2023 Iowa excludes retirement income for taxpayers age 55 or older on December 31 of the tax year, disabled taxpayers and qualifying survivors.
Under 55 (and not disabled), retirement plan distributions are taxed at the flat 3.8% rate in 2026.
The exclusion covers 401(k), 403(b) and 457(b) plans, IRAs (traditional and Roth), SEP and SIMPLE IRAs.

Iowa law provides for a flat tax rate of 3.8 percent. In 2026, all levels of taxable individual income will be subject to this rate.

Age measured at the end of the tax year.

new_york.name: New York

rate.note: 2025 IT-201 rate schedules: 10.9% over $25,000,000. Lower brackets not extracted.

exclusions.covers: Qualifying pension and annuity income: periodic and lump-sum IRA payments; periodic 401(k) distributions; periodic distributions from governmental 457 plans; periodic 403(b) distributions; Keogh payments; employee periodic pension payments.
exclusions.note: Only amounts received after reaching 59½ count. Separate full subtraction (IT-201 line 26) for NYS/local government and federal government pensions, not age-limited.

rules: New York's pension and annuity income exclusion is up to $20,000 per person, available only for amounts received after age 59½.
Lump-sum 401(k) distributions are not listed as qualifying (only periodic 401(k) distributions are); lump-sum and periodic IRA payments qualify.
Only governmental 457 plans are listed; private 457(b) plans are not.
Pensions from New York State or local governments and the federal government are subtracted separately in full on line 26.
quotes: If you became 59½ during 2025, enter only the amount you received after you became 59½, but not more than $20,000.
You may not take a pension and annuity income exclusion that exceeds $20,000, regardless of the source of the income.
periodic and lump-sum payments from an IRA, but not payments derived from contributions made after you retired
periodic distributions from government (IRC § 457) deferred compensation plans

georgia.name: Georgia

exclusions.covers: Retirement income (incl. taxable IRA and pension distributions); up to $5,000 may be earned income
exclusions.note: Also available under 62 if permanently and totally disabled. Each spouse qualifies separately. Figures from the 2025 IT-511 booklet.

rules: Georgia's retirement income exclusion starts at age 62: up to $35,000 (62-64) and $65,000 (65+) per person.
Under 62 and not permanently disabled, retirement plan distributions are fully taxable in Georgia.
Each spouse must qualify separately; up to $5,000 of the exclusion may be earned income.
quotes: exclusion is $35,000 for taxpayers who are: A. 62 - 64 years of age
The maximum retirement income exclusion is $65,000 for taxpayers who are 65 years of age or older.
The Georgia income tax rate has been reduced to a flat rate of 4.99%.

new_jersey.name: New Jersey

rate.note: 2025 rate schedules: 10.75% on income of $1,000,000 and over.

exclusions.covers: Pension/retirement exclusion (line 28a) on taxable pensions, annuities, IRA withdrawals reported on line 20a
exclusions.note: Age 62+ (or blind/disabled) on the last day of the year AND NJ income (line 27) of $150,000 or less. Max: $100,000 MFJ, $75,000 single/HOH, $50,000 MFS if income ≤ $100,000; 50% / 37.5% / 25% of line 20a for $100,001-$125,000; 25% / 18.75% / 12.5% for $125,001-$150,000; none above $150,000. Joint filers: only the pension income of the spouse who is 62+ can be excluded.

rules: New Jersey has no state additional tax on early distributions, but no retirement exclusion before age 62 (unless blind/disabled).
401(k) contributions were not taxed by New Jersey when made, so 401(k) distributions are generally fully taxable.
Employee contributions to 403(b), 457 and other plans (other than 401(k)) were taxed by New Jersey when made and are recovered tax-free on withdrawal.
IRA contributions were generally taxed when made; earnings and amounts rolled over tax-free are taxable when withdrawn (Worksheet C).
The Three-Year Rule applies to contributory pension plans: if contributions are recovered within 36 months, payments are not taxed until contributions are recovered.
The exclusion requires New Jersey income of $150,000 or less.
quotes: You (and/or your spouse if filing jointly) were age 62 or older or blind/disabled as defined by Social Security guidelines on the last day of the tax year
Your income on line 27 is $150,000 or less
Employee contributions to federal Thrift Savings Funds, 403(b), 457, SEP, or any other type of retirement plan other than 401(k) Plans.
If all of your contributions were made on or after that date, your distributions are fully taxable unless your contributions exceed the federal limit.
Do not report pension and annuity payments as income on line 20a until you have recovered all of your contributions.

exclusions.covers: Qualified retirement income from the taxpayer's own plan (IRC 401, 403, 408, 457, public plans)

rules: South Carolina's retirement deduction is up to $3,000 per year before age 65 and $10,000 from age 65.
Any portion of a distribution that triggered the federal premature-withdrawal penalty does not qualify for the deduction.
Qualified retirement income covers IRC 401, 403, 408 and 457 plans.
From tax year 2026, H. 4216 sets rates of 1.99% (under $30,000) and 5.21% minus $966 ($30,000 and above).
quotes: An individual who is under age 65 may claim a retirement deduction up to $3,000 on qualified retirement income from their own plan.
Any portion of qualified retirement income received this tax year that resulted in a federal premature withdrawal penalty does not qualify for a retirement deduction.
Qualified retirement income is income from plans defined in IRC 401, 403, 408, and 457
The tax rate for income from $30,000 and above is 5.21%, minus $966.

washington.name: Washington

rate.note: No individual income tax in 2026. Senate Bill 6346 (2026) creates a 9.9% income tax on adjusted gross income over $1 million starting Jan. 1, 2028 (first returns April 2029). Capital gains excise tax (RCW 82.87): 7% on long-term gains above the standard deduction, plus 2.9% on Washington capital gains over $1 million (9.9% total) starting tax year 2025.

rules: Washington does not currently have an individual income tax, so 401(k)/IRA distributions are not taxed by the state.
Assets held in 401(k), 403(b), 457(b), IRA and Roth IRA accounts are exempt from the capital gains excise tax.
Capital gains excise tax: 7% on long-term capital gains above the standard deduction ($278,000 for 2025; $270,000 for 2024), plus an additional 2.9% on gains over $1 million from tax year 2025.
A new 9.9% income tax on adjusted gross income over $1 million takes effect January 1, 2028 (SB 6346).
quotes: Washington does not currently have an individual income tax.
Beginning Jan. 1, 2028, a new 9.9% income tax will apply to individuals and married couples filing jointly with annual adjusted gross income exceeding $1 million.
Any amount of Washington capital gains exceeding $1 million is subject to a 7% tax, plus an additional 2.9% tax.
The standard deduction for 2025 is $278,000.
Assets held under a retirement savings account under Title 26 U.S.C. Sec. 401(k) of the internal revenue code
